guide.name: Paintball 2.1
guide.summary: A 3 minute, 2 team paint fight: throw paintballs to colour blocks for your team and hit enemies to knock them out. The team with more paint points at the end wins.
guide.tokenLine: 11, or 14 if your team wins, plus 3 or 4 for 5 players per team

beats.caption: Throw paintballs to paint blocks
beats.sub: Each block you paint that isn't your team's colour yet scores 1 point, even ones the other team painted.

beats.caption: Most paint points after 3 minutes wins
beats.sub: When they paint over your blocks, your team keeps the points it already got.

beats.caption: 14 tokens if your team wins, 11 if not
beats.sub: 5 players per team get 3 or 4 more, but which 5 is effectively random, not by score.

howToPlay.text: Players are split into 2 teams (the second team gets the extra player if the count is odd), and the teams get a random colour pair such as Red and Blue. Your inventory is saved and cleared, you get a stack of 16 paintballs in your team colour, and you glow in that colour.
Throwing a paintball paints the block it lands on, and also paints the block you are standing on when you throw.
Paintballs fly at 40% of a normal snowball's speed, and by default you can throw one every 0.2 seconds.
You never run out: each time one of your paintballs lands, your hand is reset to a full stack, and an empty hand is refilled every second.
A paintball that hits an enemy deals 12 damage (6 hearts). Teammates can't be hit.
When you knock out an enemy, your team paints a ball of blocks around where they fell and you get a kill. Knocked out players don't really die: they are put back at full health at their team spawn.
You have Regeneration II and glowing, refreshed every second. Standing in water knocks you out and sends you back to your spawn.
Your action bar shows your team's share of the painted blocks (Good Guys), the other team's share (Bad Guys), and your kill count.
After 3 minutes you see the Game Over title with the winning team and both team scores, you are sent back to the spawn, and your inventory is given back.

scoring.text: You and your team get 1 point for every block you paint that isn't already your team's colour. That counts fresh blocks and blocks the other team painted.
Painting a block your team already owns gives nothing.
Points are never taken away. When the other team paints over your block, your team keeps the point it already got for it.
Some blocks can't be painted: barriers, ladders, air, non-solid blocks, doors, trapdoors, fence gates, buttons, levers, signs, pressure plates, and blocks with water right above them.
A knockout paints a whole ball of blocks around the victim, and each of those blocks scores 1 point under the same rules.
Kills are counted on your action bar but are worth no points on their own.
Your points are added to your all-time Paintball 2.1 leaderboard total.

tokens.text: Tokens are paid once, when the game ends, to everyone still on a team, even with 0 points. If you leave early you are removed from your team and get nothing.
You get 14 tokens if your team won and 11 if it lost. On each team, the first 5 players the game counts get a bonus on top: 4 for the 1st and 3 for the 2nd to 5th.
Worked example: on the winning team the bonus players get 18 or 17 tokens and everyone else 14. On the losing team the bonus players get 15 or 14 and everyone else 11.
A staff multiplier is applied to that number and rounded, then the server-wide multiplier (1 by default) is applied and rounded up. Any single payout above 20 is cut to 20.

tips.text: Every throw also paints the block under your feet, so keep moving onto blocks that aren't your colour while you throw.

Painting over the other team's blocks is worth the same 1 point as a fresh block, and your team never loses points when they paint over yours. The winner is the team that painted the most over the whole game, not the team holding more of the map at the end.
A knockout paints a whole ball of blocks at once. 2 hits (24 damage against 20 health) knock out an enemy, as long as they haven't healed much in between.
Your tokens don't depend on your own score, only on whether your team wins (3 tokens more), so helping your team out-paint the other one is what pays.

quirks.text: The bonus is meant to go to each team's top 5 scorers, but the game puts the sorted list into an unordered map before counting positions. Which 5 players get the bonus is effectively arbitrary and doesn't follow your score.

The action bar percentages show how much of the currently painted map each team holds, but the winner is decided by total paint points, which count every block ever painted. The team ahead on the action bar can still lose.
The token formula has a cap of 25, but the most it can ever give is 18.
Paint isn't real: the blocks don't change, and the paint is only shown to players who are inside the arena when it's painted.
If both teams end on the same points, one of them is still named the winner and paid as one.
Freeze Tag uses this same token formula, but passes in its own scores instead of positions.

config.text: The blocks that can't be painted (by default doors, trapdoors, fence gates, buttons, levers, signs, and pressure plates) are a server setting.
The throw cooldown is 4 ticks by default and is a server setting.
Team spawns, the beds shown in team colours, and the arena are set per map. The 3 minute length is fixed in the code.

guide.name: Boat Race 2
guide.summary: A raft race over 3 laps through a set of checkpoints. You score points and tokens on every lap, based on your position when you cross the finish line.
guide.tokenLine: Every lap: 3 if you are top 5 at the line, otherwise 2

beats.caption: Race 3 laps through the checkpoints
beats.sub: Drive through every checkpoint, then cross the finish line to complete a lap.

beats.caption: Every lap scores on your place
beats.sub: Each lap scores the starters plus 1 minus your place, so with 8 starters 1st gets 8 and 8th gets 1.

beats.caption: 3 tokens a lap in the top 5, else 2
beats.sub: You are paid at every lap crossing, so a 3 lap race pays 6 to 9 tokens.

howToPlay.text: You are put in a bamboo raft at a random starting spot (players beyond the number of spots start near an overflow point), and the race starts right away with a Go! title.
You can't get out of your boat or teleport until you finish.
Drive through the checkpoints, then cross the finish line to complete a lap. Your boss bar shows your lap and how far through the lap's checkpoints you are.
Your action bar shows your live position and how many seconds are left.
After your last lap (3 by default) you get a Finished title with your place, chat announces it, and you are moved to the spectator area. Outside a boat inside the race area you get Speed V.
The race ends when every racer still online has finished, or after 5 minutes. Anyone still racing then is given their current place but earns nothing more.
At the end you see the Game Over title and the points table, and you are sent back to the spawn.

scoring.text: Each time you complete a lap you score the number of players who started, plus 1, minus your position at that moment. In a race with 8 starters, 1st scores 8 points for that lap and 8th scores 1.
Lap points add up into the end-of-game table and your all-time Boat Race leaderboard total.
A lap you haven't finished when time runs out scores nothing.

tokens.text: Boat Race pays tokens on every lap you complete, not once per game: its token formula is set up so it doesn't mark you as already paid.
Each lap pays 3 tokens if you are in the top 5 when you cross the line, and 2 otherwise.
Worked example with 3 laps: 9 tokens if you are top 5 at every crossing, 6 if you never are, and 7 or 8 in between.
If you leave mid-race you keep the tokens from laps you already completed. Laps not completed pay nothing.
Staff and server multipliers are applied to each lap's payout separately. For example, at a 1.5x staff multiplier a top 5 lap pays 4.5 rounded to 5.

tips.text: Your position counts at every lap crossing, not just the last one, for both points and tokens. A strong start keeps paying even if you get passed later.
Being 5th or better when you cross the line is worth 1 more token that lap than 6th or lower.
Keep going even when you are far behind: every lap you finish still pays at least 2 tokens.

quirks.text: The Game Over title names the player with the most total points, not the first across the line. Since points come from every lap, a player who led the early laps can be named the winner over the player who finished first.

When staff run a flat payout game (the broadcast says everyone gets a set number of tokens, regardless of score), Boat Race pays that flat amount on every lap, so a full race pays 3 times the announced amount.
Everyone races in a bamboo raft. The code has a random boat type, but it's switched off.
A 15 second Game Over bar after the race is meant to send everyone to the drop-off point, but by then the game has already emptied its player list, so nobody is moved.

config.text: The number of laps is 3 by default and is a server setting, which also changes the token total.
The checkpoints (2 plus the finish line by default), starting spots, overflow point, and spectator area are set per map.
The 5 minute limit is fixed in the code.

guide.name: TNT Tag
guide.summary: Hot potato tag with TNT: whoever is holding the TNT when each 90 second round ends explodes and is out. Runners score a point for every 30 seconds they go without being tagged.
guide.tokenLine: 1 per 30 seconds untagged as a Runner

beats.caption: Stay away from the Tagger
beats.sub: As a Runner you get 1 point for every 30 seconds in a row you go without being tagged.

beats.caption: A tag hands you the TNT
beats.sub: Tag someone to pass it on. A tag resets your count, and Taggers explode when the 90 second round ends.

beats.caption: 1 token per point
beats.sub: Paid when the game ends. Never tagged in all 3 rounds is 9 points, so up to 9 tokens.

howToPlay.text: Everyone starts as a Runner, and your inventory is saved and cleared. At the start of each round, 1 Tagger is picked at random for every 5 Runners (at least 1), and chat says who is it.
Runners get Speed II and glow. Taggers get Speed IV, Dolphin's Grace, a TNT block on their head, and red leather armour.
As a Tagger, hit a Runner to pass the TNT: you become a Runner and they become the Tagger. Hits deal no damage, and both players have to be inside the arena.
Each round lasts 90 seconds. When it ends, every Tagger explodes and becomes a Spectator: invisible, hidden from other players, and given Speed V. Spectators can leave with /event quit.
The next round starts straight away and everyone still playing is teleported near the spawn. The game ends after 3 rounds, or early if fewer than 2 Runners are left after a round.
If every Tagger goes offline, a random Runner becomes the Tagger.
At the end you see the Game Over title and the points table, you are teleported to the spawn, and 15 seconds later to the drop-off point.

scoring.text: As a Runner you get 1 point for every 30 seconds in a row that you go without being tagged.
Getting tagged resets that count: when you pass the TNT on and become a Runner again, you start from 0.
If you are never tagged, your count carries over from one round to the next.
Taggers and Spectators earn nothing.
Your points are added to your all-time TNT Tag leaderboard total.

tokens.text: You get 1 token per point, paid when the game ends. Spectators are paid too, for the points they earned before they exploded.
0 points pays nothing.
If you leave after the game has started, you are paid for the points you have at that moment.

Worked example: a Runner who is never tagged in all 3 rounds (270 seconds) earns up to 9 points, so up to 9 tokens. A Runner tagged once in the middle of each round loses the progress toward the next point every time.

tips.text: Being the Tagger when the round timer hits 0 knocks you out, so watch the Round ends in bar and pass the TNT before it runs out.
There is no cooldown on tagging back, so the Runner you just tagged can tag you straight back. Get away from them first.
Points only come from long untagged stretches, and every tag resets your count, so staying away from the Tagger matters more than anything else.

quirks.text: The game's internal time limit is 9 minutes, twice what the 3 rounds take, so the rounds always end the game first.
With 2 to 9 Runners there is only 1 Tagger. With exactly 2 players the game ends after round 1, since only 1 Runner is left.

config.text: A fresh server only has an empty default TNT Tag map with no arena or spawn set, so the game can't start until staff set one up. A map only sets the spawn point and the arena.
The round length, number of rounds, tagger ratio, and 30 second point timer are fixed in the code.

guide.name: Towers
guide.summary: Free-for-all PvP where everyone starts on their own 1-block bedrock pillar and gets a random item every 9 seconds to build and fight with. Each kill is worth 1 point, and you get 1 more point for either dying or lasting to the end.

howToPlay.text: Join with /event join while the queue is open (90 seconds by default). At least 2 players are needed. Your inventory is saved and cleared when the game starts and given back when it ends.

Each player gets their own pillar: a column of bedrock from just under your spawn down to the bottom of the world. The first pillar is at the center and the rest are placed in rings around it, at least 20 blocks apart. Your health and hunger are filled at the start.
A 3 second "Get ready!" countdown plays, then "Go!". Until then you are slowed so you can't move and you can't jump.
At "Go!" and then every 9 seconds (the "Next drop in" bar), every player still in gets an item dropped at their eyes, and chat says "You got: <item> x<amount>".

Most drops (79%) are 3 or 4 of a random solid block. About 12% are one of 10 kits: TNT (3 TNT and a redstone torch), food (an enchanted golden apple, 6 cooked beef and 3 cakes), a bow with 3 arrows, 3 wind charges, an ender pearl with an end crystal, 3 cobwebs, 15 eggs (5 of each color), a diamond sword kit (3 diamonds, a stick and an oak log), a happy ghast egg with a green harness, or a warden egg with a sculk catalyst. The other 9% is 1 random item from a pool of tools, weapons, armor, spawn eggs, beds and similar.
Right-click a spawn egg in the air to throw it. The mob spawns where the egg lands and counts as yours.
You can craft in your own 2 by 2 grid and at a crafting table, but other containers such as chests and furnaces can't be opened.

You are out when you die, from any cause. The death message is shown to the game, you stay alive as an invisible flying spectator, and you can't interact, drop items or pick items up. Spectators who drift below the arena are pulled back above it.

Kill credit goes to the last player who damaged someone, and it isn't cleared over time. A hit that knocks a player off their tower counts as your kill when they die.
Throw spawn eggs by right-clicking the air. Using one on a block spawns a normal mob that isn't tied to you, so its hits give you no kill credit.
The diamond sword kit is a crafting kit: turn the log into planks and a crafting table, then craft a diamond sword from 2 diamonds and the stick.
Drops are thrown at your eye position as an item rather than put straight into your inventory, so stay on your tower when the "Next drop in" bar runs out.

quirks.text: The "has won!" title at the end names the player with the most points, which is the player with the most kills, not necessarily the last one standing.

A mob thrown by a player who is now out (or a tagged mob whose owner is gone) dies as soon as it hits someone.
The random single-item pool includes every spawn egg in the game, so a large share of those drops are spawn eggs.
Map configs have Ivory and Scarlet center points that Towers never uses, and there is a separate Towers token formula with a cap of 15 that the game doesn't use (it uses the 9 cap).

Pillars must fit within 250 blocks of the center by default.
The 10 kits and the single-item pool are the defaults and can be changed per map.
The server-wide token multiplier is 1.0 by default.

beats.caption: Build out from your pillar
beats.sub: You start on your own 1 block pillar. Every 9 seconds you get a random item, most often 3 or 4 blocks.

beats.caption: Knock players off their towers
beats.sub: When a player dies, whoever hit them last gets the kill and their whole inventory.

beats.caption: Your tokens are your kills + 1
beats.sub: The +1 is for dying or for lasting to the end, so only kills earn more. Up to 9.

guide.name: Manor
guide.summary: A 1-Hunter tag game. Shrunken Runners try not to get caught in the dark while the Hunter catches them with 1 hit, and Runners score for time survived while the Hunter scores for each catch.

howToPlay.text: Join with /event join while the queue is open. At least 2 players are needed. Your inventory is saved and cleared for the game, and you can't move items or switch hotbar slots.
1 random player becomes the Hunter. Everyone else is a Runner and is sent to the start point. The Hunter waits at the waiting spot for 15 seconds, then is sent to the start point too.
Runners wear boots that shrink them to half size, and get Darkness, Glowing and Night Vision.
The Hunter gets Glowing, Night Vision and Speed I. Runners can only see the Hunter when they're within 7 blocks of them.
The Hunter can see a Runner who is within 6 blocks or 15 or more blocks away, but not one in between.
Runners within 30 blocks of the Hunter hear a Warden heartbeat that gets louder, higher and faster the closer the Hunter is.
1 hit from the Hunter catches a Runner. Runners can't hit anyone ('You cannot attack this player.').
A caught Runner becomes an invisible spectator at the start point. Each catch adds 15 seconds to the game, unless it was the last Runner.
Once the Hunter spawns, a boss bar shows how many Runners are left.

The game ends when the Hunter catches every Runner, or when time runs out (2 minutes 15 seconds plus any added time). If the Hunter leaves, a random Runner takes over, and if fewer than 2 players are left the game ends. At the end the top 5 scores are posted and you're sent back to the waiting spot.

scoring.text: Runners get 1 point about every 40 seconds while they're still Runners, counting from the very start of the game (the 15 seconds before the Hunter spawns included).
The Hunter gets 1 point for each catch.
Caught Runners keep their points but earn no more as spectators. A Runner who takes over as Hunter keeps their Runner points.
Your score is also added to your all-time Manor total, which feeds the server's top 10 leaderboard.

tokens.text: You're paid once, when the game ends: your score plus 2, up to 15.
Caught Runners stay in the game as spectators and are paid at the end like everyone else.
Example: in a game with no catches, a Runner lasts the full 2 minutes 15 seconds and gets 3 points, so 5 tokens. A Runner caught in the first 40 seconds has 0 points and gets 2.
Example: a Hunter who catches 6 Runners gets 6 + 2 = 8 tokens. The 15 token cap is reached at 13 points.

The event's usual rules then apply: staff can start a game that pays a multiple of this, a flat amount for everyone, or nothing (announced in chat). The server's token multiplier is applied and rounded up, and you receive at most 20 Soul Orbs from one payout.

numbers.label: Heartbeat
numbers.value: Within 30 blocks; about every 1.1 s at the edge down to every 0.4 s up close, volume 0.4 to 2.0

tips.text: Runners: when the Hunter is 6 to 15 blocks away they can't see you at all. Closer than 6 or farther than 15, they can, and you're Glowing.
If you can see the Hunter, they're within 7 blocks of you.
Use the heartbeat as a distance meter: silence means the Hunter is more than 30 blocks away, and the faster it beats the closer they are.
Every catch except the last adds 15 seconds, which also gives the Runners still in the game more time to earn points.

quirks.text: When time runs out there's no message saying the Runners won. Only a Hunter clean sweep gets an announcement ('The hunter has caught all runners. The hunter wins...').

'This minigame has concluded.' is sent when the game stops. The 15 second Game Over bar after it is meant to send everyone to the drop-off point and say it again, but the game has already emptied its player list by then, so nothing happens and you stay at the waiting spot.

The game only handles catches by the Hunter. Deaths from anything else aren't stopped by the game, so they'd be a normal death. Whether the map has anything that can hurt you depends on the map. Not tested here.

config.text: Manor's map file starts with 1 map entry with no locations filled in, so the server has to set it up before Manor can be played.
The waiting spot, start point and play area come from the map config, which has the same shape as Prop Hunt's.
Manor isn't in the default automatic rotation.

beats.caption: Stay 6 to 15 blocks from the Hunter
beats.sub: The Hunter can't see you in that band, only closer or farther out. 1 hit from them catches you.

beats.caption: Stay uncaught to score
beats.sub: You get 1 point about every 40 seconds. Each catch gives the Hunter 1 point and adds 15 seconds.

beats.caption: Your score plus 2 tokens
beats.sub: Paid once at the end, up to 15. A Runner with 3 points gets 5, and a Hunter with 6 catches gets 8.

guide.name: Prop Hunt
guide.summary: Hide and seek with disguises. Hiders turn into blocks and hide in the map while Seekers hunt them down, and Hiders score for time survived while Seekers score for each catch.
guide.tokenLine: Your score, at least 3 and at most 13

howToPlay.text: Join with /event join while the queue is open. At least 2 players are needed. Your inventory is saved and cleared for the game, and you can't move items or switch hotbar slots.
1 random player becomes the Seeker and gets a Stone Sword and Speed I. Everyone else is a Hider and is sent to the start point, while the Seeker waits at the waiting spot for 40 seconds.

As a Hider, left-click a block to disguise yourself as it. It has to be a solid, non see-through block (stairs and slabs also work), and not a barrier. After disguising you must wait 22.5 seconds before picking another block.

While disguised, right-click a block to lock in place. The space you're standing in must be empty: a real block of your disguise is placed there, and you sit invisible next to it (on top if there's room), hidden from Seekers. Sneak to get off and unlock.
After 40 seconds the Seeker is sent to the start point, everyone hears a Warden emerging, and a 5 minute timer starts.
A Seeker catches a Hider with 1 hit. Left-clicking a locked Hider's block unlocks them and hits them in the same click. Seekers can't hurt other Seekers or spectators, and Hiders can't hit anyone.
Every 22.5 seconds the Seeker hears a sound at each Hider's position: a Warden listening sound at the nearest Hider and clicking sounds at the rest. Only the Seeker hears these.
A caught Hider has a 20% chance to become another Seeker. Otherwise they become an invisible spectator. Either way they're sent back to the start point.
Only a Seeker's hit can take you out; any other death is prevented. Your hunger stays full.

The game ends when every Hider is caught (Seekers win) or the 5 minute timer runs out (Hiders win). If no Seeker is left, a random Hider becomes the Seeker. At the end the top 5 scores are posted and you're sent back to the waiting spot.

scoring.text: Hiders get 1 point every 40 seconds while they're still Hiders, counting from the very start of the game (the 40 second hiding time included).
Seekers get 1 point for each Hider they catch.
Caught Hiders keep the points they earned. Spectators earn nothing more, and a Hider who becomes a Seeker adds catches on top of their Hider points.
Your score is also added to your all-time Prop Hunt total, which feeds the server's top 10 leaderboard.

tokens.text: You're paid once, when the game ends: your score is your token count, but never less than 3 or more than 13.
Caught players who became spectators stay in the game and are paid at the end like everyone else.

Example: a Hider who's never caught is in the game for the full 5 minutes 40 seconds and earns 8 points, so 8 tokens. A Seeker who catches 5 Hiders gets 5 tokens, and one who catches only 1 still gets 3.
Example: a Hider caught at 2 minutes (3 points) who becomes a Seeker and catches 4 more ends on 7 points, so 7 tokens.

The event's usual rules then apply: staff can start a game that pays a multiple of this, a flat amount for everyone, or nothing (announced in chat). The server's token multiplier is applied and rounded up, and you receive at most 20 Soul Orbs from one payout.

numbers.label: Seeking time
numbers.value: 5 min, so 5 min 40 s in total

tips.text: Seekers: the sound tells you which Hider is closest. The Warden listening sound is the nearest one, and the clicks are everyone else.
Locked Hiders give off block particles from their block every 0.5 seconds, so Seekers should watch for blocks shedding particles, and Hiders should know a locked spot isn't silent.
Hiders: locking is what hides you from Seekers. Unlocked, you're a moving block that Seekers can see and hit.
Hiders score just by staying uncaught, so surviving the whole game (8 points) beats any early catch. Seekers need 4 or more catches to earn more than the 3 token minimum.
When you lock, a real block of your disguise type appears where you stand, so pick a disguise that matches the blocks around your hiding spot.

quirks.text: The message says you can only disguise as solid, opaque blocks, but stairs and slabs are allowed too.
The end title says '<name> has won!' for whoever has the most points, which can be a Seeker even when the Hiders won.
'Time is up! Hiders win!' is sent by the 5 minute timer after it stops the game. The game's own time limit ends at the same moment, and if that one fires first, the message may not appear.
The nearest Hider's clue sound is played quieter (0.8) than the other Hiders' sounds (2.0).
While you're looking at another unlocked Hider within 6 blocks, your clicks as a Hider do nothing, so you can't disguise or lock until you look away.
A code comment says the 40 second hiding time is meant to become 30 seconds.
There's a switched-off handler that would lock you in place when you stop sneaking. It isn't active, so locking is right-click only.

After the game a 15 second Game Over bar runs. When it ends it's meant to send you to the drop-off point and say 'This minigame has concluded.', but the game has already emptied its player list by then, so nothing happens and you stay at the waiting spot.

config.text: The waiting spot, start point and play area come from the server's Prop Hunt map file, which has the same layout as Manor's. A new map file starts with 1 map entry with no locations filled in, so the server has to set it up.
Prop Hunt only starts if the server has the LibsDisguises plugin, which it uses for the block disguise.
Prop Hunt isn't in the default automatic rotation.
How far the Seeker's clue sounds carry is up to the game's normal sound rules. Not tested here.

guide.name: The Nabbits
guide.summary: A spreading tag game: one player starts as the Nabbit and catches fleeing players with 3 hits each. Caught players turn into Nabbits or Rabbits, and the fleeing players win if anyone is still uncaught after 6 minutes.
guide.tokenLine: 1 per point, max 10 (the end-of-game payout is broken)

beats.caption: Run from the Nabbit
beats.sub: It catches you with 3 hits. Each carrot you walk over has a 1 in 10 chance to give 1 point.

beats.caption: Caught? Become a Nabbit or Rabbit
beats.sub: It's 50/50. Nabbits score 1 point per catch, and everyone scores 2 points per full minute.

beats.caption: The end payout is broken
beats.sub: It should pay 1 token per point, up to 10, but players still in at the end get no tokens in this version.

howToPlay.text: Everyone starts as Fleeing and is sent to a random spot in the play areas, and your inventory is saved and cleared. One random player becomes The Nabbit, and chat tells everyone to run.
Nabbits glow dark purple and have Speed I, refreshed every second.
A Nabbit catches a Fleeing player by hitting them 3 times. Stars on the action bar show how many hits you have taken. Hits deal no damage.
A caught player has a 50% chance to become a Nabbit and a 50% chance to become a Rabbit (disguised as a small rabbit).
Rabbits can't be caught and can't hit Nabbits. Their job is collecting carrots.
2 carrots spawn every second at random spots. Fleeing players and Rabbits pick them up by walking over them (they don't go into your inventory). Nabbits can't pick them up.
Every 15 seconds all Fleeing players glow for 1 second in a random colour, showing where they are. Your action bar counts down to the next reveal.
Throwing projectiles and eating chorus fruit are blocked.
If every Nabbit goes offline, a random Fleeing player or Rabbit becomes the new Nabbit.
The game ends with Nabbits Win when no Fleeing players are left, or with Fleeing Players Win after 6 minutes.

scoring.text: Nabbits score 1 point for each player they catch.
Everyone, in every role, scores 2 points for each full minute in the game.
Fleeing players and Rabbits: each carrot picked up has a 1 in 10 chance to give 1 point.
Winning gives no extra points.

tokens.text: The token formula pays 1 token per point, up to 10.
In this version, players still in the game when it ends are not paid. The game clears its player list before the end-of-game payout looks you up, so you get no tokens and no leaderboard score.
As written, time points alone (2 per minute) would reach the 10 token cap after 5 minutes.

tips.text: Nabbits always glow, so you can always see where they are. Fleeing players only show up during the reveal every 15 seconds, so be out of a Nabbit's sight when your action bar countdown hits 0.
Hits on you never reset, so 2 hits taken early still count later in the game.
As a Nabbit, 1 catch is worth as much as 10 carrots on average.

quirks.text: End-of-game payout is broken in this version: the game empties its player list before paying, so nobody still playing at the end receives tokens or leaderboard score, even though the points table is shown.
Each role has a score multiplier in the code (1.2 for The Nabbit, 0.8 for other Nabbits, 0.5 for Rabbits, 1.0 for Fleeing), but nothing uses it.
The Rabbit title says "Collect carrots to score points", but each carrot only has a 1 in 10 chance to give a point.
Time points go to every role, so getting caught doesn't cost you the 2 points per minute.

config.text: A fresh server only has an empty default Nabbits map with no arena or spawn set, so the game can't start until staff set one up. It also won't start unless the server has the LibsDisguises plugin, which the Rabbit disguise uses.
A map sets the spawn, the arena, and the play areas (2 by default) where players and carrots spawn.
The 6 minute length, 3 hits to catch, and 15 second reveal are fixed in the code.

guide.name: Panel Party
guide.summary: A last-player-standing floor game: each round a block is called, every other block of the floor is removed, and anyone not standing on the called block falls. Your tokens come from how many panels you survive, with a bonus for the purple rounds at the end.
guide.tokenLine: 1 per 2 panels survived, +1 per purple panel, max 13

howToPlay.text: Join with /event join while the queue is open (90 seconds by default). Panel Party can start with just 1 player. Your inventory is saved and cleared when the game starts and given back when it ends.
Everyone is teleported to the same spot near the middle of the first panel. You can't place or break blocks during the game.
Each round is a new panel (a floor pattern). The map has a list of panel designs, they are shuffled at the start, and each one is played once, so the game has as many rounds as the map has designs.

When a round starts, chat and your action bar show "Stand on: <block>" in that block's color, and a bossbar shows the panel's name and round number while it counts down. In green and yellow rounds you are also handed the called block so you can see it.

When the bossbar runs out, every block that isn't the called block is removed and a 5 second "Don't move!" bar starts. You need to be standing on the called block by then. After that the next panel is pasted and the next round starts.
The rounds get harder in 4 equal parts of the game: the first quarter of rounds are green (11 seconds to find the block), then yellow (7 seconds), then red (6 seconds), then purple (4 seconds).
Purple rounds are PvP rounds. During their "Don't move! (PvP)" phase, players who are still in can hit each other. At any other time, hits between players are cancelled.

You are eliminated if you fall 50 blocks below the panel or die. You then become a spectator: you're teleported 10 blocks above the middle, you can fly, you're invisible, and players still in the game can't see you. Chat shows a random elimination message such as "<name> chose a bad block."

howToPlay.text: The game ends when 1 player (or nobody) is left, with "<name> was the last player standing!", or when the last panel is done ("No more panels left to play!"). The top 5 scores are then shown in chat, and after a 10 second "Game Over" bar you are sent back.

scoring.text: Every player still in when a round's "Don't move!" bar ends gets points: 1 for a green or yellow round and 2 for a red or purple round.
The last player standing gets 1 bonus point.
Being eliminated earns nothing. A line that would have given 1 point on elimination is commented out.
Points decide the end-of-game ranking and are added to your all-time Panel Party leaderboard score, but they don't decide your tokens. Tokens count panels survived instead (see below).

tokens.text: You are paid once, when the game ends, and spectators who were eliminated are paid too. If you leave with /event quit during the game, you are paid right then for what you have survived so far.

If the server sees you AFK for 6 minutes, a warning bossbar counts you down, and at 7 minutes you are removed from the game and get no tokens. This also counts while you spectate after being knocked out, so move now and then. Bedrock players are skipped.
Tokens = panels survived divided by 2 (rounded down), plus 1 for each purple panel survived, up to 13.

Example with a 12-panel map: rounds 1-3 are green, 4-6 yellow, 7-9 red and 10-12 purple. If you survive all 12, you get 12 / 2 = 6 plus 3 for the purple panels, so 9 tokens. If you fall in round 8, you survived 7 panels, so 7 / 2 = 3 tokens.
Winning doesn't add tokens. The last-player bonus only goes to the scoreboard.

Staff can start a game with a token multiplier (applied after the 13 cap), a flat amount for everyone, or no tokens, and chat announces it. Then the server-wide multiplier is applied, rounded up, and you get at most 20 tokens from one payout.

tips.text: Green and yellow rounds only call blocks that cover at least 10 blocks of the playable area. From the red rounds on, any block in the playable area can be called, even one that appears only once, so expect much smaller targets late in the game.
In red and purple rounds you aren't handed the block, so read the "Stand on" text in your action bar.
Purple panels are worth the most: 2 points and 1 full token each, on top of the usual 1 token per 2 panels. Making it into the last quarter of rounds is the biggest jump in pay.
In purple rounds other players can hit you while the floor is gone, so keep away from other players during the "Don't move! (PvP)" bar.

quirks.text: The token formula's description says "1 token per 2-3 panels survived", but Panel Party always uses 2 panels per token.

The game ends as soon as 1 player is left, and the round in progress isn't counted. So the winner usually ends with the same number of panels survived, and the same tokens, as the last player to fall.
If several players reach the end of the last panel, the game ends with "No more panels left to play!" and nobody gets the last-player bonus point.

In about 30% of games, the colored terracotta in every panel is swapped for wool of the same color, so you are told to stand on wool instead. Plain terracotta stays as it is. The code calls this "glazed", but the swap is to wool.
The bossbar names each panel after its design file in quotes, with "and" shown as "&".
There is code for a round type that gives Jump Boost, but none of the 4 round types use it.

config.text: The list of panel designs is set per map (empty by default), and it sets how many rounds there are.
The playable area used to pick which blocks can be called is 64 by 64 blocks by default (a radius of 32).
Super speed is on by default: you get Speed with an amplifier of 255, refreshed every tick. If a map turns it off, all your potion effects are cleared every tick instead.
The server-wide token multiplier is 1.0 by default.

beats.sub: Each round names 1 block. Get onto it before the bar runs out: 11 seconds at first, 4 at the end.

beats.caption: Every other block is removed
beats.sub: For 5 seconds only the called block is left. Anyone not standing on it falls and is out.

beats.caption: 1 token per 2 panels survived
beats.sub: Plus 1 per purple panel, up to 13. Surviving a 12-panel map pays 9. Winning adds nothing.

guide.name: MineBattle
guide.summary: A free-for-all mining and PvP game. Everyone starts sealed in their own small pocket inside a big block of deepslate, mines ores for random gear, books and effects, and fights whoever they run into. Points come from staying alive and from kills, and the game ends when 1 player is left or the time runs out.
guide.tokenLine: 1 per point (1 a minute alive, 2 a kill), max 12

howToPlay.text: Join during the queue and you are sent to the MineBattle lobby. Your inventory is saved and cleared when the game starts and given back when it ends. The game needs at least 2 players or it is cancelled.

When it starts, the game builds a fresh arena sized to the number of players: a box of mostly deepslate with random ores, wrapped in a layer of reinforced deepslate and then bedrock. A yellow "Generating Arena..." bar runs for 5 seconds while this happens.

Each player is then teleported into their own 3x3x3 air pocket somewhere inside the arena, spread apart from the others, and given a stone sword and a diamond pickaxe (Efficiency III, Unbreaking X). Both starting tools have Curse of Vanishing. Chat then says "MineBattle started!".
While you are alive you always have Night Vision and your hunger is kept full.

You can only see another living player if they are within 10 blocks and there is no solid, opaque block between your eyes and theirs. Within 2 blocks you always see each other. Anyone further away is hidden from you completely. This is rechecked about 4 times a second.

Plain deepslate drops nothing. Ores give a reward straight into your inventory instead of their normal drop: cobbled deepslate gives 1 gray stained glass, coal gives a random chainmail armor piece, iron gives a random iron armor piece or an iron sword, diamond gives a random diamond armor piece or a diamond sword, ancient debris gives a random netherite armor piece or a netherite sword, redstone gives 1 TNT, and a raw gold block gives a golden apple.

Lapis gives an enchanted book, picked evenly from 14 options: Sharpness I or II, Feather Falling III, Protection I or II, Blast Protection I, II or III, Knockback I or II, Thorns I, II or III, or Curse of Vanishing.

To use a book, pick it up on your cursor and click it onto a sword or armor piece in your inventory. Sharpness and Knockback only go on swords, Feather Falling only on boots, and Protection, Blast Protection and Thorns only on armor. If the book's level matches the item's current level, the item goes up 1 level.
Copper changes your max health by 1 heart, up or down on a coin flip. The change stacks each time you mine copper and lasts until you are eliminated or the game ends.
Gold ore lets you see every other living player within 25 blocks for 3 seconds. They glow for 3 seconds and hear a wither sound. It does nothing while an all-player reveal is already running.

Emerald gives you a random potion effect, or raises one you already have by 1 level: Absorption (up to V), Haste (up to III), Resistance (up to II), and Strength, Fire Resistance, Invisibility, Jump Boost and Speed (level I only). Once every effect is at its max you get a "Caution!" warning, and mining another emerald after that kills you.
Placing TNT lights it straight away with a 2 second fuse. You can also place the gray stained glass you get from cobbled deepslate.

When you die you are eliminated: everything in your inventory without Curse of Vanishing drops where you died, and you become a spectator (spectator mode, invisible to the players still fighting). Spectators who fly more than 200 blocks from the arena are pulled back.
The player who killed you gets Regeneration III for 5 seconds and a "+1 kill" message with their kill total.

The game ends as soon as 1 or no players are left alive, or when the time limit (6 minutes by default) runs out. Everyone sees a "Game Over" title, the top 5 by points are listed in chat, the arena is removed and you are sent back to the MineBattle lobby with your own inventory.

scoring.text: You get 1 point for every full 60 seconds you stay alive. The clock only runs once the arena is ready, and spectators do not earn it.
You get 2 points for each kill. The kill goes to the player who caused the death, so TNT you placed is credited to you (the game sets you as the TNT's source). Killing yourself scores nothing.
Nothing else gives points. Mining, being the last player alive and lasting until the timer ends are not rewarded on their own.
Your points from each game are also added to your all-time MineBattle total, which feeds a top 10 MineBattle leaderboard.

tokens.text: Tokens are paid when the game ends, to everyone who took part, including players who were eliminated and are spectating. You get 1 token per point, capped at 12.
0 points means 0 tokens, so someone killed in their first minute without a kill gets nothing.

Example: you survive 4 minutes, get 1 kill, then die. That is 4 + 2 = 6 points, so 6 tokens. Example: you survive the whole default 6 minute game (5 survival points) and get 4 kills (8 points). That is 13 points, capped to 12 tokens.

Staff can start a game with a token multiplier, a flat payout for everyone, or no tokens at all, and the server has its own multiplier on top (rounded up). A single payout is capped at 20 tokens, but the chat message shows the amount before that cap.
You can only be paid once per game.

tips.text: A kill is worth as much as 2 minutes of survival, and survival tops out around 5 points in a default game, so you need kills to get near the 12 token cap.
Only solid, opaque blocks block sight. The gray stained glass from cobbled deepslate does not hide you, so wall yourself in with deepslate instead.
Mine ores by hand. Blocks destroyed by TNT drop nothing, and ore rewards only come from breaking the block yourself.
Two books of the same enchantment and level add up: put Sharpness II on a sword that already has Sharpness II and it becomes Sharpness III.
Your starting sword and pickaxe never drop, but everything you mined does. Killing a well geared player leaves their armor and books on the ground for you.
If you suddenly glow and hear a wither sound, someone within 25 blocks mined gold ore and can see you for the next 3 seconds.
Stop mining emeralds once you see the "Caution!" message. The next one kills you.
Copper is a gamble: half the time it takes a heart away.

quirks.text: The "Game Over" title names whoever has the most points as the winner, not the last player alive.

Emerald effects are meant to last until the game ends, but their timer starts when the game is announced, not when it starts. With the default 90 second queue they wear off about 80 seconds before the time limit, and an emerald mined in the last 90 seconds gives an effect that lasts only 10 seconds.
Protection and Blast Protection can both go on the same armor piece, which normal Minecraft does not allow.
The Curse of Vanishing book can be put on any sword or armor piece, and that item then stays out of your death drops.
Books cannot go on the pickaxe. Clicking a book onto anything other than a sword or armor is treated as a normal inventory click.
The "Time is up!" message never shows. The game stops on its own clock about a second before the green "Time Left" bar reaches 0, and stopping the bar skips that message.

After the 10 second blue "Game Over" bar you are supposed to be sent to the event drop-off point with a "This minigame has concluded." message, but the player list is already cleared by then, so you stay in the MineBattle lobby and get no message.
There is unused code for earning survival points gradually over the whole time limit. It does the maths but never adds the points, so only the 1 point per minute counts.

config.text: The time limit is 360 seconds by default.
Sight range is 10 blocks with line of sight and 2 blocks without, by default.

Timed reveals are off by default. When on, every living player glows and is visible to all for 3 seconds at half time, 5 seconds with a quarter left, 10 seconds with an eighth left, and for the rest of the game with a sixteenth left (22.5 seconds in a 6 minute game).

A shrinking world border is off by default. When on, it starts just outside the arena and shrinks to 5 blocks wide over the time limit, dealing 3.5 damage per second for each block you are outside it.

By default the arena is 80% plain deepslate, 5% coal, 3.92% cobbled deepslate, 3% iron, 2.2% each copper and redstone, 1.2% each gold and lapis, 0.6% each diamond and emerald, and 0.04% each ancient debris and raw gold block.
Arena radius (10 to 32 blocks), height (32), spacing between spawn pockets (12 blocks) and padding from the walls (3 blocks) are defaults the server can change.

If the server has MineBattle structure files installed, each player has a 50% chance that a random structure is placed in their spawn pocket, and they spawn in an extra empty pocket instead. Without those files there are no structures.

MineBattle uses the shared minigame AFK check: if the server's AFK tracker sees you idle for 6 minutes you get a warning, and after 7 minutes you are removed with no tokens. With the default 6 minute time limit MineBattle always ends first, so this only matters if staff set a longer limit.

guide.name: TNT Run
guide.summary: A survival game on a floor that crumbles under your feet: every sand-like block you step on disappears 1 second later. Your score and tokens grow with every second you stay up, and the game ends when 1 player is left.

howToPlay.text: Join with /event join while the queue is open (90 seconds by default). At least 2 players are needed. You wait in the lobby, and your inventory is saved and cleared when the game starts and given back when it ends.
The arena is rebuilt from scratch, then everyone is teleported in and a 10 second "Starting in" bar runs. When it ends, chat says "TNT Run started!" and the floor starts to fall apart.

Any block affected by gravity (like sand or gravel) that you step on disappears 1 second later, and if there is TNT directly under it, the TNT goes too. Other blocks never disappear. Standing still doesn't stop it, because the game also marks the blocks under your feet 4 times a second.
Powerups appear on the floor as small spinning items. Walk into one to pick it up, then right-click it to use it.

The powerups are Slow Falling (phantom membrane), Jump & Speed (rabbit foot), Small Updraft (feather) and Big Updraft (firework rocket), which launch you upward, and Temporary Platform (bedrock), which puts a 3 by 3 bedrock platform under you.
When the game starts you are also handed 1 of each of the 5 powerups, but they only work once "TNT Run started!" shows.

You are out when you drop below the elimination height. Chat says "You have been eliminated!", you're sent back into the arena as a flying spectator, and you're invisible and hidden from the other players.
The game ends when 1 player (or nobody) is left, or when the "Time Left" bar runs out ("Time is up!"). The top 5 scores are shown, then a 10 second "Game Over" bar runs before you are sent back.

scoring.text: You get 1 point every 0.25 seconds you are still in the game, so 4 points per second.
Points start as soon as the arena is ready, so the 10 second "Starting in" countdown already gives everyone about 40 points.
Your score stops when you are eliminated. There is no bonus for winning, so your score is simply how long you lasted.
Your score is also added to your all-time TNT Run leaderboard score.

tokens.text: Tokens = your score divided by 90, rounded down, up to 12. Since you score 4 points a second, that's 1 token for every 22.5 seconds you last.

Examples: out 1 minute after "TNT Run started!" is about 40 + 240 = 280 points, so 3 tokens. Lasting 2 minutes is about 520 points, so 5 tokens. The cap of 12 needs 1,080 points, about 4 minutes 20 seconds after the start.
You are paid once, when the game ends, and eliminated spectators are paid too. If you leave with /event quit during the game, you are paid right then for your score so far.

Staff can start a game with a token multiplier (applied after the 12 cap), a flat amount for everyone, or no tokens, and chat announces it. Then the server-wide multiplier is applied, rounded up, and you get at most 20 tokens from one payout.

A code comment says the token formula still needs fixing.
The game's damage protection only works while the join queue is open, not during play.

guide.name: Freeze Tag
guide.summary: A 2 team tag game: hit enemies to freeze them in ice and hit frozen teammates to free them. A round ends when one whole team is frozen, and the first team to win 2 rounds wins the match.
guide.tokenLine: 11, or 14 if your team wins, plus up to 5 more for a low score

beats.caption: Hit an enemy 3 times to freeze them
beats.sub: Hits deal no damage. The hit that freezes them scores you 6 points.

beats.caption: 4 hits frees a frozen teammate
beats.sub: That scores you 4 points. A round ends when every player on one team is frozen.

beats.caption: 14 tokens if your team wins, 11 if not
beats.sub: A low score adds up to 5 more, so a player on 0 points is paid 5 more than one on 6 or more.

howToPlay.text: When the game starts, players are shuffled and split into 2 teams (Scarlet and Ivory by default). With an odd number of players the second team gets the extra player. You get a leather chestplate and a glow in your team colour, and you are sent to your team's spawn.
Hits never deal damage. Hit an enemy 3 times to freeze them. Each hit before the last one knocks them back a little.

A frozen player is locked in a block of ice and glows. They can still look around, but any movement snaps them back to where they were frozen. Their teammates get a chat message asking them to unfreeze them.
Hit a frozen teammate 4 times to unfreeze them. The ice cracks a bit more with each hit.
Hitting a teammate who isn't frozen but has taken freeze hits heals them by 1 hit.
While you are frozen you can't freeze enemies or unfreeze teammates, but by default you can still heal teammates who come to you.
Your action bar shows how many players on each team are frozen, and in the middle either your hearts (hits left before you freeze) or, while frozen, the snowflakes left until you are free.

A round ends as soon as every player on one team is frozen, and the team with more unfrozen players wins it. After 5 seconds everyone is unfrozen, all hits are cleared, and the next round starts from the team spawns.

The match ends when a team reaches 2 round wins, or when the 6 minute timer runs out. The timer is for the whole match, not each round. On time out the team with more round wins wins, and if round wins are tied the team with more unfrozen players at that moment wins. If that is also equal it's a tie.
Your inventory is saved and cleared when the game starts and given back at the end. After the Game Over title you stay where you are in the arena.

scoring.text: You score 6 points for the hit that freezes an enemy. Only the hit that completes the freeze scores, not the hits before it.
You score 4 points for the hit that unfreezes a teammate.
Healing scores nothing, and you never lose points.
At the end your score is added to your all-time Freeze Tag leaderboard total.

tokens.text: Tokens are paid once, when the match ends, to every player still on a team. If you leave before the end you are taken off your team and get nothing.

Freeze Tag pays with the Paintball 2.1 token formula. Your score is passed in where that formula expects a finishing position: you get 14 tokens if your team won and 11 otherwise, plus 5 if your score is 0, 4 if it is 1, 3 if it is 2 to 5, and nothing extra if it is 6 or more.

Worked example with the default points (6 per freeze, 4 per unfreeze): on the winning team you get 19 tokens with 0 points, 17 with 4 points, and 14 with 6 or more. On the losing team, or when nobody wins, that is 16, 14, and 11.
A staff multiplier is applied to that number and rounded, then the server-wide multiplier (1 by default) is applied and rounded up. Any single payout above 20 is cut to 20.

numbers.label: Round wins to win the match

tips.text: Freeze hits on an enemy stay counted until they are frozen, healed, or the round resets, so an enemy a teammate already hit twice needs just 1 more hit. The 6 points go to whoever lands that last hit.
If you have taken freeze hits, let a teammate hit you: each hit takes 1 off. By default even a frozen teammate can do this, so standing next to a frozen teammate is a way to heal.
A round only ends when every player on a team is frozen at the same time, so as long as you keep unfreezing teammates your team can't lose the round.

quirks.text: Freeze Tag has its own token formula (a minimum plus tokens per point), but the game never uses it. It builds the Paintball 2.1 formula instead and feeds your score in as if it were a finishing position, so a higher score never earns more tokens: by default a player with 0 points is paid 5 more than a player with 6 or more.
The server settings minimumTokens (5) and tokensPerPoint (1) look like they control the payout, but nothing reads them.

When the timer runs out with round wins tied, the Game Over title picks the winner by who has more unfrozen players. Tokens are worked out after everyone has been unfrozen, so the winner's 14 base goes to the team with more players left in the game (or to nobody if the teams are the same size). The team named on screen can miss out on the winner's tokens.
The join title says "Freeze all enemy players to win!", but freezing everyone only wins the round. By default your team needs 2 round wins.
The check that ends a round skips a team with no players, so if everyone on one team leaves, the round can't end by freezing and the match runs until the timer.
After the Game Over title a 10 second bar runs that is meant to send everyone to the lobby, but by then the game has already emptied its player list, so nobody is moved.

config.text: Team names and colours are Scarlet (red) and Ivory (white) by default.

The time limit (360 seconds), hits to freeze (3), hits to unfreeze (4), round wins needed (2), and points per freeze and unfreeze (6 and 4) are server settings, so the live values may differ. Because the token payout depends on your score, changing the points also changes who gets the bonus.
By default frozen players can't freeze enemies or unfreeze teammates but can heal. Each of these 3 rules is a server setting.
The team spawns and the arena are set per map.

guide.name: Soccer
guide.summary: A 2 team ball game on a pitch. You push a Sulfur Cube ball into the other team's goal. Scoring a goal or winning a round on plays is worth 10 points, and the first team to 30 points wins.
guide.tokenLine: 3 + 1 per 2 plays, +2 if your team is ahead, max 15

howToPlay.text: Join during the queue and you are sent to the Soccer spawn. Your inventory is saved and cleared for the game. You cannot move items, switch hotbar slots or drop anything while playing.

At the start, players are shuffled and split into 2 teams, taking turns, so the teams differ by at most 1 player. The matchup is picked at random: Red Team vs Blue Team, Team KitKat vs Team Oreo, or Team Mayo vs Team Mustard. You wear a leather chestplate in your team's colour.
With a big crowd, more than 1 ball is used and chat announces how many are in play.

Each round starts with everyone teleported near their team's start point and frozen in place (no walking or jumping) for a countdown: 5 seconds before the first round, 3 before the rest. On "GO!" the balls appear and the 90 second round clock starts.
During the game you have Speed IV and Strength II and your hunger is kept full. Your action bar shows the speed of the nearest ball, your own speed, and your latest play.
You move the ball by running into it. The faster you are running at it, the harder it goes, and if several players touch it at once the one running at it fastest gets the push.
You can only punch the ball when you are within 9 blocks (by default) of your own goal. Anywhere else the punch does nothing and you see "You can only punch the ball near your own goal!".
Particles mark both goals for you: red dust on the goal you defend, green dust on the goal you attack. Only you see your markers.

A round ends when a ball goes into a goal, when a ball leaves the pitch, or when the 90 seconds run out. After a goal or a timed out round, everyone within 35 blocks of that spot is launched away from it, and the next round starts 3.5 seconds later. After a ball leaves the pitch, the next countdown starts straight away.
Hitting other players does no damage.

If the server's AFK tracker sees you idle for 6 minutes, you get an "Are you still there?" title and a red "You are AFK!" bar counting down. Move within 1 minute or you are removed from the game. Bedrock players are not checked.

The game ends when a team reaches 30 points, or after 20 minutes. Everyone sees a "Game Over" title naming the leading team, team scores are listed in chat, your chestplate is removed and you are sent back to the Soccer spawn.

scoring.text: Goal: when a ball goes into a goal, the last player who touched it decides who scores. If it is the other team's goal, your team gets 10 points and you get a Goal play. If it is your own goal, the other team gets 10 points.
Round on plays: if the 90 seconds run out with no goal, the team that made more plays that round gets 10 points. If both teams made the same number, nobody scores.
Out of bounds: if a ball leaves the pitch, the team of the last player to touch it loses 2 points. A team never drops below 0, and the other team gets nothing.

Plays are your personal score. Each of these is worth 1 play to you and 1 to your team's count for the round: First touch (the first bump on a fresh ball), Air hit (bumping the ball while it is in the air), Save (touching the ball while it is within 2 blocks of your own goal or flying at it from up to 12 blocks away, by bump or punch), Power kick (the ball reaches 40 blocks per second within 0.6 seconds of your bump or punch) and Goal.

scoring.text: The same play again within 0.75 seconds does not count, but different plays from one touch all count, for example a First touch that is also an Air hit.
With more than 1 ball, only the first goal or out of bounds in a round counts. The other balls are removed, and a goal another ball scores after that does nothing.
Your plays are added to your all-time Soccer total, which feeds a top 10 Soccer leaderboard. They are not shown on the end screen.

tokens.text: Tokens are paid when the game ends to every player still in it: 3 tokens, plus 1 for every 2 plays you made (rounded down), plus 2 if your team is ahead when the game ends, with a minimum of 3 and a maximum of 15.
The winning bonus only goes to a team that is strictly ahead. If the scores are level, or nobody has any points, nobody gets the bonus.
Leaving early, with /event quit, by disconnecting or by being removed for being AFK, gives up all your tokens for that game.

Example: 7 plays on the losing team is 3 + 3 = 6 tokens. 12 plays on the winning team is 3 + 6 + 2 = 11 tokens. 0 plays still gets 3 tokens. 24 or more plays on the winning team hits the 15 token cap.

Staff can start a game with a token multiplier, a flat payout for everyone, or no tokens at all, and the server has its own multiplier on top (rounded up). A single payout is capped at 20 tokens, but the chat message shows the amount before that cap.
You can only be paid once per game.

tips.text: A round with no goal still gives 10 points, the same as a goal, to the team with more plays. When a goal is not coming, keep getting touches (first touches, air hits, saves) before the 90 seconds run out.
Stand in the ball's path to stop it. A ball moving under 40 blocks per second stops when it reaches a player and counts as that player's touch. Faster shots pass straight through players.
A body push tops out at 32 blocks per second, below the 40 a Power kick needs, so a push on its own will not earn one.
Defenders can punch and attackers cannot, since punching only works near your own goal. A punch that stops a ball heading for your goal also counts as a Save.
The last touch decides everything: who scores, whether it is an own goal, and which team pays the out of bounds penalty. Be careful clearing the ball near your own goal or the sidelines.
Stay until the end. Everyone still in the game gets at least 3 tokens, and leaving gives up all of them.
Run at the ball rather than walking into it: your speed towards it sets how hard it goes, and in a crowd the fastest runner wins the push.

quirks.text: An own goal's chat message says "-10 points", but your team does not lose anything. The other team gains 10 points instead.
If a team that has 0 points knocks the ball out, chat still prints a "Penalty" line, but it shows 0 points.
If the ball reaches a goal before anyone has touched it, nothing happens and play goes on.
Goals are checked once per tick rather than along the ball's path, so the ball has to actually be inside the goal at one of those checks to count.
The "Game Over" title always names a winner. On a tie it names one of the teams anyway (but nobody gets the winning bonus), and if no team ever scored it says "Unknown has won!".
The code has a "Times up, game over!" message for the 20 minute limit, but it never shows because the game stops before it can run.

After the 15 second blue "Game Over" bar you are supposed to be sent to the event drop-off point with a "This minigame has concluded." message, but the player list is already cleared by then, so you stay at the Soccer spawn and get no message.
The game can start with just 1 player. The code marks this as a placeholder to be raised to 2.

config.text: Punch range is 9 blocks from your own goal by default.
Each map sets its own pitch edges, goals, team start points and ball spawn, so pitch size and goal size depend on the map.
Extra balls spawn in a ring around the centre spot, 18% of the pitch's shorter side away, kept between 3 and 12 blocks.
Soccer is in the default list for automatic games (with Bomberman and Incursion), but automatic games are switched off by default.

beats.sub: The first team to 30 wins. If 90 seconds pass with no goal, the team with more plays gets 10.

beats.caption: 3 tokens + 1 per 2 plays
beats.sub: Plus 2 if your team is ahead at the end, up to 15. Leaving early gives up all of them.

guide.name: Incursion
guide.summary: A two-team shooter where you score by diving into the enemy team's hole, with kills worth a smaller bonus. After 8 minutes the team with the higher total score wins, but your tokens come only from your own points.

howToPlay.text: Join with /event join while the queue is open (90 seconds by default). At least 2 players are needed or the game is cancelled. You are sent to the lobby, and your inventory is saved and cleared, then given back when the game ends.
Players are split into 2 teams, Scarlet and Ivory, with team sizes at most 1 apart. By default the split also tries to give both teams a similar average ping, with a little randomness.

Your kit is a team-coloured leather chestplate plus 4 weapons in hotbar slots 1 to 4: Last Resort (stone sword, Sharpness II), Overwatch (spyglass), Blunderhorn (goat horn) and Spitter (pufferfish). You can't take off the chestplate, rearrange your inventory, drop items or swap hands.
At the start everyone is sent to a random spot in their team's spawn area and frozen for 5 seconds while a "Get ready" countdown plays. Nobody can deal or take damage until "GO!" shows.

Your goal is to reach the enemy team's hole and jump into it. That scores for you and your team, then sends you back to your own spawn. Jumping into your own hole says "That's your own hole! No points for you." and sends you back, and so does leaving the arena ("Don't leave the arena!").

Overwatch: hold right click to charge, and release once the title shows READY (a bell plays) to fire a beam. It passes through every enemy in a line and stops at the first solid block. Letting go early fires nothing ("The shot wasn't fully charged!"), and switching hotbar slot cancels the charge.
Blunderhorn: right click for a short cone blast that hits every enemy inside it who isn't behind a wall. It hurts less the further away they are.
Spitter: right click to spit a stream of water that flies in an arc (aimed a little above your crosshair) and hits the first enemy it touches.

Overwatch, Blunderhorn, Spitter and the eggs deal true damage: it comes straight off health and ignores armor. They can only hurt the enemy team and Vanguards, never your own team. Hitting teammates with the sword is also blocked.

Orbs (dark particle spheres with a white core) float around the map. Walk through one to get a random egg: Unstable Egg (blast only), Cryo Egg (blast plus frost and slowness) or Incendiary Egg (blast plus fire). Throw it and it goes off where it lands. An orb comes back 30 seconds after someone takes it.

Some maps have boss rooms, each guarded by a Vanguard (a Drowned with a trident by default, its HP shown on its name tag). It stays locked in its room and attacks the nearest player in range. Killing it drops 2-5 random eggs on the floor, and it comes back 60 seconds later.

When you die there is no death screen. You go straight back to your spawn area at full health, frozen for 2.5 seconds and invincible for 2.5 seconds (a ⛨ timer and a ring of team-coloured particles). While invincible you can't use your weapons or eggs either.

At 4 minutes it is half time: the teams swap sides, every orb refills, every Vanguard respawns, and everyone gets a fresh 5 second countdown at their new spawn. Chat warns you 60, 30, 10, 3, 2 and 1 seconds before the swap and before the end.

Don't go AFK. After 6 minutes without moving you get an "Are you still there?" warning with a countdown bar, and at 7 minutes you are removed from the game. Players removed for being AFK get no tokens.

Your action bar always shows both team scores and your own points ("You: 150"). The game ends after 8 minutes. The team with the higher score is announced as the winner, then you are sent to the lobby and get your inventory back.

scoring.text: Diving into the enemy hole gives 100 points to you and your team.

Killing an enemy gives you 25 points. If they die without a direct killer (a long fall, fire, a Vanguard), the kill goes to the last enemy who damaged them, as long as that was within the last 10 seconds.
Killing a Vanguard gives 0 points by default. You only get the eggs it drops.
Nothing takes points away. Dying, jumping into your own hole or leaving the arena only cost you the trip back to spawn.
Your team's score is every point its members earned, and it never goes down, even if a player leaves. It only decides which team is named the winner.
When you are paid, your points from the game are also added to your all-time Incursion leaderboard score.

tokens.text: You are paid Soul Orbs when the game ends, once per game.
The formula is 3 tokens plus 1 for every full 75 points you scored, capped at 13. So 0 points gives 3 tokens and 750 points or more gives the full 13.
Example: 1 hole and 2 kills is 150 points, which is 3 + 2 = 5 tokens. 4 holes and 6 kills is 550 points, and 550 / 75 rounds down to 7, so 10 tokens.
There is no win bonus. Only your own points count, so you get the same tokens whether your team wins or loses.
Staff can start a game with a token multiplier (the result is rounded, so 10 tokens at 1.5x becomes 15), a flat amount for everyone, or no tokens at all. Chat says which when the game is announced.
After that, the server-wide token multiplier (1 by default) is applied and rounded up, and a single payout can't give more than 20 tokens.

tips.text: A hole is worth 4 kills, so diving is the fastest way to tokens. 1 hole is 100 points, which is already more than 1 token on its own.
Dying never costs points, only about 2.5 seconds stuck at spawn, so an aggressive dive that fails costs you very little.

Overwatch headshots do 28 damage, more than the normal 20 health, so one headshot kills a player at full health. The head zone is the top part of the hitbox, from a little below eye level up. A body shot does 14.
The Overwatch beam pierces, so lining up 2 enemies hits both of them.
Wait for the bell and READY before letting go of Overwatch. An early release fires nothing, but it also doesn't start the cooldown, so you can charge again straight away.
The Blunderhorn does 25 damage at point blank, enough to kill a full-health player in one blast, but only 3.75 at its 6.5 block edge. Get right up close before using it.
Knocking an enemy off a drop of 10 or more blocks kills them, and you get the 25 points if you hit them in the last 10 seconds. Every custom weapon and the eggs push players back.

Eggs go off in real time and need a clear line to you, so stepping behind a wall saves you from the blast. Overwatch, Blunderhorn and Spitter shots are judged by where you were a moment earlier (the shooter's ping plus 120 ms, up to 300 ms by default), so ducking into cover at the very last moment may not save you.
Vanguard eggs land on the floor and anyone can pick them up, enemies included, so grab them quickly. Killing a Vanguard gives no points by default, so only fight it if you want the eggs.
Every orb refills at half time, so it's worth checking them again at the start of the second half.

quirks.text: With an odd number of players the bigger team is slowed down from the very first second, because the slowdown only looks at team sizes. In a 3 vs 2 game the team of 3 moves 15% slower, and chat tells both teams about it.
When players leave mid-game, their team keeps every point they earned, and the other team, now the bigger one, is slowed down until the numbers even out.
Barrier blocks don't stop anything: Overwatch beams, Blunderhorn blasts, Spitter streams and egg blasts all go through them as if they weren't there.
Killing a Vanguard is announced to everyone as "defeated a vanguard! (+0)", because by default it is worth 0 points.
If both teams finish on the same score, the end screen still names one of them as the winner ("... has won!"). Nothing in the code breaks the tie.
Vanguards only burn when an Incendiary Egg hits them. Sunlight and other fire don't hurt them.
The server config's comment on points per token says you can earn up to 11 tokens, but the formula actually caps at 13.

config.text: Each Incursion map can be switched on or off, and a random enabled map is picked when the game starts. Incursion is also in the default list of games that start automatically.
Team names and colours are Scarlet (red) and Ivory (white) by default.

Game length (8 minutes), start countdown (5 seconds), respawn freeze (2.5 seconds), respawn invincibility (2.5 seconds) and a movement speed multiplier (1, so normal speed) are all set per map by default.
Hole points (100), kill points (25), Vanguard points (0) and points per token (75) can be changed per map. The 3 token base and 13 token cap are fixed in code.
The outnumbering slowdown is on by default: 25% at double the other team's size, at most 40%, and anything under 2% is ignored. The code never allows more than 60%.

Ping-based team balancing is on by default. Lag compensation is on by default too, rewinding shots by the shooter's ping plus 120 ms, up to 300 ms (the code never rewinds more than 800 ms whatever the setting).
Every weapon and egg stat in the numbers above (damage, range, cooldown, falloff, knockback, effect lengths) is a per-map setting, so the live values may differ.

Orb spawn spots, boss rooms and the Vanguard's mob type (Drowned with a trident by default, or a bow-using Parched or a potion-throwing Witch), health, respawn time and egg drop count are set per map. A map with no boss rooms has no Vanguards.

beats.sub: Get past the other team and jump into their hole. That's 100 points, then you go back to your spawn.

beats.caption: Kills add 25 each
beats.sub: Taking down an enemy is 25 points, so a hole is worth 4 kills. Nothing ever takes points away.

beats.caption: 3 tokens plus 1 per 75 points
beats.sub: Up to 13. 1 hole and 2 kills is 150 points, so 5 tokens. Only your own points count, win or lose.

guide.name: Bomberman
guide.summary: A last-one-standing bombing game over 2 rounds, in an arena the game builds to fit the number of players. You drop TNT to blow up soft blocks and other players, and your points for blocks, kills and round wins decide your tokens.
guide.tokenLine: 3 to 13 by how close you get to the target score, +2 for a round win, max 13

howToPlay.text: Join with /event join while the queue is open. Bomberman starts with as few as 1 player. Your inventory is saved and cleared when the game starts and given back at the end.

Each round a fresh arena is built: a bedrock floor, unbreakable obsidian pillars, and soft blocks 7 high everywhere else, in a random one of 7 block themes. Everyone starts at their own spawn, spread out toward the edges and facing the middle, and is held still with Slowness for 1 second.

howToPlay.text: Your kit is 64 TNT, a diamond pickaxe, a diamond axe and 64 cooked porkchops. You start at full health with Mining Fatigue II, and you can't jump. You can't drop items.

Place TNT anywhere in the arena to drop a lit bomb with a 1.5 second fuse. You can only have 1 bomb out at a time, and the next one is ready as soon as it explodes. Your TNT stack is topped back up to 64 each time.
A bomb removes the whole soft-block column (all 7 blocks) for every column the blast reaches within 2 blocks of it, measured flat. Pillars and the floor can't be destroyed, and nothing drops.
You can also mine soft blocks with your tools. A column only counts as cleared once all 7 of its blocks are gone. Pillars and the floor can't be mined.
Other players' bombs are the only danger from other players: hitting someone does nothing, your own bomb can't hurt you, and explosions don't knock players back.
You only see other living players when they're within 5 blocks of you or nothing solid (a soft block or pillar) stands between you on the grid. They see you by the same rule.

When you would die, you're healed and turned into an invisible, flying spectator who can't be hurt and can't place or break blocks. If you fell off the map, you're put 32 blocks above the arena centre.

howToPlay.text: A round ends when 1 player is left (or nobody is), or when the 3 minute timer runs out.

If the timer runs out with 2 or more players alive, Sudden Death starts: every soft block is removed, the survivors are healed, re-equipped and moved to spots around the centre, and they get 60 seconds to finish it. If more than 1 is still alive after that, nobody wins the round.

After round 1 there's a 10 second break showing who won, then round 2 starts in a new arena with everyone back in, eliminated players included. After round 2 the top 5 scores are posted in chat, a title names the top scorer, and the game ends 10 seconds later.

scoring.text: +1 for each soft-block column your bomb destroys.
+1 for each column you clear by hand, counted when you break its last block.
+60 for each player your bomb kills, as long as you're still alive when they die.
+30 for winning a round by being the last one standing.
Nothing takes points away. Your score carries over from round 1 to round 2.
Your score is also added to your all-time Bomberman total, which feeds the server's top 10 leaderboard (refreshed every minute).

tokens.text: You're paid once, when the game ends, from your total score. Eliminated players are still in the game as spectators and are paid the same way.

If you stay AFK for 7 minutes you're removed from the game (after a warning from 6 minutes), and you get no tokens and no leaderboard points. This counts for spectators too. Idle time only counts from the start of the game, so in practice it can only happen late in a game that had a Sudden Death. Bedrock players are exempt.

tokens.text: You get 3 tokens, plus up to 10 more as your score climbs toward a target score, plus 2 if you won at least 1 round. The total never goes above 13.

The target is set once, at the start of round 1: twice your fair share of the arena's soft columns plus 60 for every other player, doubled for the 2 rounds. In other words, clearing twice your share of blocks and killing everyone in both rounds.

Example with 4 players: the arena is 32 blocks wide with about 708 soft columns (worked out from the arena template), so the target is 1,068. Clearing 150 columns, getting 1 kill and winning 1 round is 240 points, which is 22% of the target: 3 + 2 + 2 for the win = 7 tokens.
Same game, 400 columns, 3 kills and 2 round wins is 640 points (60%): 3 + 6 + 2 = 11 tokens. A round winner reaches 13 from 801 points; without a round win you need 1,015.

The event's usual rules then apply: staff can start a game that pays a multiple of this, a flat amount for everyone, or nothing (announced in chat). The server's token multiplier is applied and rounded up, and you receive at most 20 Soul Orbs from one payout. The chat message shows the amount before that 20 cap.
