tips.text: Bomb rather than mine. A bomb clears whole 7-block columns several at a time, while mining needs all 7 blocks of a column broken for 1 point, and you have Mining Fatigue II.
A kill is worth 60 points, as much as 60 columns, and a round win adds 30 more. The 2 token win bonus is the same whether you win 1 round or both.
Your own bomb can't hurt you and blasts don't push you, so standing next to your own bomb is safe.
If you're eliminated before your bomb goes off, that bomb earns you nothing: no block points and no kill.
Walls hide you as well as your opponents. Every column you clear opens sight lines, and anyone within 5 blocks can see you regardless.
Sudden Death removes every soft block, so from then on only kills and the round win score.

quirks.text: One of the possible subtitles when you join is leftover placeholder text: '// TODO: Splash Text'.
If the player whose bomb killed you was already eliminated, chat says you 'blew themselves up!', even though your own bomb can't hurt you.
The end-of-game title names the player with the most points, who isn't always the player who won the most rounds.
The +2 win bonus is cut off by the 13 token cap, so it adds only 1 token if your score alone gets you 12, and nothing if it gets you 13.
Playing alone, you win every round you survive to the end of the timer, since the round only ends early if nobody is left.

A code comment says the arena width must be 17, 21, 25 and so on (steps of 4) for the pillar grid to line up, but the minimum width is 32. Worked out from the arena template, games with 1-5 players get a lopsided pillar grid, with pillars along the north and west edges but not the south and east.

config.text: The waiting spot and the arena's centre point come from the map config. The arena itself is generated by the game every round.
By default, Bomberman is 1 of 3 games (with Incursion and Soccer) in the automatic rotation, but automatic games are switched off by default.
The server's token multiplier is 1 by default.
Bomb damage is the game's normal TNT damage; the code doesn't change it. Not tested here.

guide.name: SkyWars
guide.summary: Team SkyWars on floating islands: loot copper chests, fight with what you find, and stay inside a border that starts closing 90 seconds in. The last team with anyone alive wins. You score for damage dealt, kills and time alive, and your Soul Orbs come from your own score, plus 1 if your team wins.
guide.tokenLine: 2 + 1 per 10 points, max 8, +1 if your team wins

howToPlay.text: Join with /event join while the queue is open (90 seconds by default). You are sent to the SkyWars lobby. At least 2 players are needed or the game is cancelled. When it starts your inventory is saved and cleared, then given back when the game ends.

Each team gets its own island. If there are no more players than islands, everyone plays solo. Otherwise teams are as small as possible (players divided by islands, rounded up), players are shuffled into them so team sizes differ by at most 1, and teams are placed on random islands. The in-game guide says maps have around 12 to 16 islands.

Your team is shown by a leather helmet in its colour (Red, Blue, Lime, Yellow and so on, 16 colours). It has Curse of Binding, so you can't take it off, and it never drops. You can always see enemy players.

While the arena is built your action bar shows "Pasting Arena" and then "Filling Chests" with a percentage. Then you are put on your island at full health and food and frozen for a 10 second countdown: you can look around but not walk, jump, break or place blocks, open anything or drop items, and nobody can be hurt. "GO!" starts the game.

Loot is in copper chests, and the more oxidized the chest, the better the loot: Copper (common), Exposed (uncommon), Weathered (rare) and Oxidized (epic). Waxed chests count the same as unwaxed ones. Every chest is filled once at the start and items are spread across random slots.

By default a Copper chest always has a stack of blocks and a stone or copper weapon, then random rolls of food, copper armor, tools, snowballs, eggs and the like. Exposed chests are all random rolls, with iron gear, bows, golden apples, lava and ender pearls in the mix. Weathered always has 1 piece of iron or diamond gear and can hold TNT, cobwebs and wind charges. Oxidized always has 1 piece of diamond or netherite gear and can hold a mace, a totem or an enchanted golden apple.

Plain chests built into the map are spare chest spots that only appear when teams are bigger: none when everyone is solo, about a third of them with teams of 2, two thirds with teams of 3 and all of them with teams of 4 or more. They are used starting with the ones nearest the map's origin point, and the nearer one is, the better its tier (the nearest quarter of the range is Oxidized, the furthest quarter plain Copper). Unused spots are left empty.
If teams end up uneven, every chest within 15 blocks of a smaller team's island spawn is bumped up 1 tier (Oxidized stays Oxidized).
You can't hurt your teammates with hits, arrows, snowballs or eggs (your action bar says "That's your teammate."). Snowballs and eggs that hit an enemy knock them back a little.

The border starts as a square around the whole map plus 2 blocks on each side, centred on the middle of the islands. 90 seconds after GO, chat says "The border is closing in! Head towards the center." with a bell, and over the next 6 minutes it shrinks to 24 by 24 blocks, where it stays.
Outside the border you take damage once a second: 1 plus 0.5 for every block you are past it, up to 8 (4 hearts) per hit.

When you die, a lightning effect hits your spot and everything you carried drops there, except your team helmet. You become an invisible, flying spectator that other players can't see. You can't hurt anyone, use or open anything, or pick items up. Fly more than 700 blocks from the map or below the world and you are sent back to your team's island.

When only one team still has a living player, that team wins. A 5 second "Game Over" bar names it, then everyone is sent to the lobby and gets their inventory back. The game lasts 10 minutes, counted from when the queue closes (so map setup and the countdown come out of it). If time runs out with 2 or more teams alive, chat says "No team won this time!"

howToPlay.text: Most commands are blocked while you play. /event (including /event quit) and chat commands like /msg, /r and /p still work. Leaving with /event quit or logging out takes you out of the game for good.

Don't go idle. While alive you get an AFK warning after 60 seconds without moving and are removed at 90 seconds. As a spectator the limits are 6 and 7 minutes. Players removed for being AFK get no Soul Orbs. Bedrock players are never removed for this.

scoring.text: Damage: 1 point for every 2 damage (1 heart) you deal to enemy players. Only damage that actually lands counts: armor reduces it, and you can't score more than the health they had left. Leftover damage carries over to your next hit.

Kills: 4 points on top of the damage points. The kill goes to whoever Minecraft names as the killer. Hitting someone with a snowball or egg also makes you their killer if they die soon after, for example by falling off the map.
Survival: 1 point every 30 seconds while you are alive. It stops when you die.
Nothing takes points away, and dying keeps the points you already have.
At the end chat shows the top 5 scores. When you are paid, your score is also added to your all-time SkyWars leaderboard score.

tokens.text: You are paid Soul Orbs when the game ends, once per game. Dying doesn't stop that: spectators are paid with everyone else.
The formula is 2 Soul Orbs plus 1 for every 10 points, rounded to the nearest whole number, up to 8 at 55 points or more. So 0 to 4 points is 2, 5 to 14 is 3, 15 to 24 is 4, and so on.
Everyone on the winning team gets 1 more, including teammates who died, for a max of 9. If time runs out with 2 or more teams alive, nobody gets the bonus.
Example: 5 minutes alive (10 points), 10 hearts of damage (10 points) and 2 kills (8 points) is 28 points, which is 2 + 3 = 5 Soul Orbs, or 6 if your team wins.
Staff can start a game with a token multiplier (rounded, so 5 at 1.5x becomes 8), a flat amount for everyone, or no tokens at all. Chat says which when the game is announced.
After that, the server-wide token multiplier (1 by default) is applied and rounded up, and a single payout can't give more than 20.

tips.text: Staying alive the whole game is only worth about 19 points (4 Soul Orbs), so you need damage and kills to get near the 8 cap. A kill where you dealt all 20 of their health yourself is worth at least 14 points (10 for damage plus 4 for the kill), whatever armor they wear.
Knocking someone off the map gets you the 4 kill points, but you only get damage points for the hits you landed, not their fall. Beating them down with your own hits is worth more.
Go for the more oxidized chests: every Oxidized chest has a guaranteed piece of diamond or netherite gear, and every Weathered chest a guaranteed piece of iron or diamond gear.

The border ends at 24 by 24 blocks around the middle of the map about 7.5 minutes after GO, so plan to be there by then. Being 6 or more blocks outside it costs 4 damage a second, and 14 or more costs the full 8.
Chests don't get refilled, and a player who dies drops everything where they died. A fight in the middle of an island leaves their loot for you to grab, but a fall into the void takes it with them.
After you die, move now and then. A spectator idle for 7 minutes is removed and gets no Soul Orbs, even though dying early still pays at the end.
The win bonus is just 1 Soul Orb and only comes if your team is the last one standing before time runs out. Dead teammates still get it, so helping a teammate survive pays off for you too.

quirks.text: There is no live score display. You only see points in the top 5 list at the end.
The end screen title says "[name] has won!" for the player with the highest score, even though the game itself is won by a team. The boss bar and chat name the winning team.
The survival clock starts when you are put on your island, before the 10 second countdown, so your first survival point comes 20 seconds after GO.
A kill still counts if you died before your victim did, for example after knocking them toward the void.
No default chest has helmets, and the bound team helmet fills your head slot anyway, so the leather team helmet is the only helmet you get.
Only your items are saved, not your XP. Enchanting with the Oxidized chest's enchanting table spends your own XP levels, and the game won't give them back.
If every other team leaves the game, your team wins straight away.

config.text: Each SkyWars map sets its lobby, schematic and origin point, and a random map is picked for each game. SkyWars isn't in the default list of games that start automatically.
Island spawns come from marker blocks in the map, so the number of islands (and so the team size) depends on the map.
Island radius for the short-handed chest upgrade (15 blocks) and the spectator range (700 blocks) are set per map.
All 4 loot tables (what each chest tier can hold, the weights and the number of rolls) are per-map settings, so the loot and odds above are only the defaults.
The game length, countdown, border timing and size, border damage, point values and the 0 to 60 score range for Soul Orbs are fixed in code.

guide.name: Manor 2
guide.summary: Hide and seek in the dark. Invisible Ghosts grab Hunters to kill them, while Hunters use a flashlight to find hidden artifacts and to light up Ghosts until they die. Ghosts win by killing every Hunter, Hunters win by killing every Ghost, and after 5 minutes it's a tie.
guide.tokenLine: 2 to 8 by score, +1 if your team wins

beats.caption: Sweep your flashlight for artifacts
beats.sub: Hold right click to shine it 8 blocks. It reveals hidden artifacts, and each one you click is 50 points.

beats.caption: Light the Ghost for 2.5 seconds
beats.sub: A grab kills a Hunter in 2.5 seconds, but your light breaks it. Hunters share 200 points for the kill.

beats.caption: 2 to 8 Soul Orbs, +1 if your side wins
beats.sub: In a full 5 minute game, 100 points or less pays 2 and 700 or more pays 8. A tie on 300 points pays 4.

howToPlay.text: Join with /event join while the queue is open. At least 2 players are needed. You're sent to the Manor 2 lobby, and chat gives you a 'Click here for more info' link to the game's How to Play page.

howToPlay.text: When the game starts your inventory is saved and cleared, and you get it back at the end. Your hunger is kept full the whole game.

Players are shuffled and 1 in every 10 (rounded up) becomes a Ghost, so 2 to 10 players have 1 Ghost and 11 to 20 have 2. Everyone else is a Hunter. Each side starts at its own spawn points, and a title tells you your role.
Ghosts are invisible, and Hunters can't see them at all unless light is on them. Ghosts see a glowing outline on every Hunter within 20 blocks.
Ghosts start with 3 cookies and get 1 more for every kill. Eating one gives Speed I for 3 seconds, with 10 seconds between cookies.
To kill, a Ghost left clicks a Hunter. Both are frozen in place, the Hunter's view is turned to face the Ghost, and after 2.5 seconds the Hunter dies. During a grab the Ghost is fully visible.
A Ghost can't start a grab while it's fully exposed by light, while it's on cooldown, or on a Hunter who was just freed from another grab.

Hunters get a Flashlight in slot 1 and red and black leather armour. Hold right click to shine it. Hunters can't hit each other, can't see other Hunters or their light, and don't hear a teammate being grabbed.

The beam reaches 8 blocks and is stopped by solid blocks. When it hits a Ghost, Hunters within 20 blocks can see that Ghost. A hit at the very edge of the beam only shows a glowing outline, and anything closer to the middle fully exposes it.
Every tick of light that fully exposes a Ghost counts toward killing it. 2.5 seconds of it in total, from any Hunters, kills the Ghost.
A Ghost stays revealed for 3 seconds after the light leaves it. After that its kill progress fades at the same rate it built up.
The map's own light reveals Ghosts too: standing in block light of 8 or more fully exposes them, and 6 or 7 shows an outline. This light doesn't count toward killing them.

Artifacts are hidden around the map. A Hunter's flashlight reveals any within 8 blocks that it has a clear line to, and a glowing item appears with 'Click on the artifact to get it'. Click it to collect it. A revealed artifact hides again after 10 seconds without light.
When an artifact is collected, a new one appears somewhere with no Hunter within 10 blocks.
A Hunter within 10 blocks of a Ghost gets colder (frost on the screen) and their flashlight flickers or blacks out, more the closer the Ghost is. The frost does no damage.

When you die, Hunter or Ghost, your soul is bound to an artifact: you shrink to about 1 block tall, turn invisible, and are moved to a spot where an artifact was collected, boxed in by a world border ('Hide from hunters!'). If no spot is free yet, you see 'Waiting for a safe region...' until one is.

If a Hunter's beam finds you as an artifact, you're frozen and an artifact item with an enchanted glint appears on you. If they click it you're out and become a spectator. If the light leaves you alone for 10 seconds, you can move again.

Spectators are hidden from everyone in the game. Your hotbar fills with the heads of up to 9 top scorers who are still playing, refreshed every 10 seconds, and eating a head teleports you to that player.
Leaving the play area shows 'Out of bounds', and after 5 seconds outside you die.
Ghosts and Hunters who go AFK get a warning at 30 seconds and are removed at 45 seconds, with no Soul Orbs.

Hunters win when every Ghost is dead and Ghosts win when every Hunter is dead. If neither happens in 5 minutes it's a tie. Everyone goes back to the lobby, the top 5 scores are posted with each player's team, and you're told your own place.

scoring.text: Ghosts get 100 points for each Hunter they kill.
Hunters share 200 points for each Ghost killed, split by how much of the killing light each one gave. Chat names every Hunter who gave more than 15% of it.
Hunters get 50 points for each artifact they collect, including dead players bound to artifacts.
Dead players earn 75 points a minute (counted continuously) while hidden as an artifact, from the moment they're placed until they're found or the game ends.
Your score is also added to your all-time Manor 2 total, which feeds the server's top 10 leaderboard.

tokens.text: You're paid Soul Orbs once, when the game ends: 2 to 8 based on your score, plus 1 if your team won. A tie pays no win bonus.
You keep your side when you die, so dead players still get the win bonus.

The score you need depends on how long the game ran. In a full 5 minute game, 100 points or less gives 2 and 700 or more gives 8, so about 1 Soul Orb per 100 points in between. A shorter game scales this down with the time played (at 4 minutes it's 80 to 560), but never below the 2.5 minute level of 50 to 350.
Example: a full 5 minute game ends in a tie. A Hunter on 300 points (6 artifacts) gets 2 + 2 = 4 Soul Orbs.

Example: a Ghost kills all 5 Hunters in 2 minutes. That counts as 2.5 minutes, so the Ghost's 500 points are past the top of 350: 8 + 1 for the win = 9 Soul Orbs. A Hunter who ends that game on 50 points gets 2.
Staff can start a game with a token multiplier (the result is rounded, so 6 Soul Orbs at 1.5x becomes 9), a flat amount for everyone, or none at all. Chat says which when the game is announced.
After that, the server-wide token multiplier (1 by default) is applied and rounded up, and a single payout can't give more than 20 Soul Orbs.

tips.text: Turn off fullbright or gamma mods, as the game's own How to Play page asks. Ghosts stay hidden either way, and the mod only stops you seeing where your own beam reaches.
Hunters: the battery refills twice as fast as it drains, so short bursts beat holding it down. The beam also gets dimmer and narrower as the battery drops.
Hunters: frost creeping onto your screen or a flickering flashlight means a Ghost is within 10 blocks.
Listen for a breeze whirl. Every Ghost makes one every 4 seconds.
Hunters: artifacts are revealed in a wider cone than your beam, so sweep your view around a room to find them.
Hunters: a Ghost that is grabbing someone is fully visible. Shine your light on it to break the grab, and the same light counts toward killing it.
Grabbed? Your own light can't break you free, but your view is locked onto the Ghost and your light still counts toward killing it.
Ghosts: stay out of lit areas. Block light of 8 or more exposes you, stops you grabbing, and lets Hunters see you from 20 blocks.
Ghosts: your health bar shows how close the light is to killing you. It drops as kill progress builds and refills as it fades, and the light never takes you below half a heart.

Ghosts: if light lands on you mid grab, letting go with your swap hands key (F by default) costs a 5 second cooldown and 1 second exposed. Being broken free costs 10 seconds, 3 seconds exposed and a knockback.
Dead? Hide well. As an artifact you earn 75 points a minute until a Hunter finds you, and you still get the win bonus if your side wins.
Hunters: an artifact with an enchanted glint is a dead player. Collecting it scores you 50 and stops them earning artifact points.

quirks.text: The 'Time Remaining' bar starts at 310 seconds, but the game ends in a tie when it reaches about 10.
The How to Play page says revealed Ghosts can't kill, but only full exposure stops a grab. A Ghost showing just an outline can still grab you.
The config has a separate 75 point setting for finding a dead player's artifact, but the code gives the normal artifact score (50) instead.

A new Ghost is only picked when a Ghost leaves the game, not when one dies. A random dead player becomes the Ghost (or a random Hunter if nobody is dead and more than 1 Hunter is left), chat says '<name> has risen as a ghost!', and they count as a Ghost for the win bonus.
The Flashlight is a trident made to look like a spyglass, and throwing it is blocked.

config.text: Each Manor 2 map sets its own lobby, Hunter and Ghost spawn points and play area, and a random map is picked when the game starts. Manor 2 isn't in the default list of games that start automatically.
By default a game lasts 5 minutes, there is 1 Ghost per 10 players, 2.5 seconds of light kills a Ghost, and Ghosts see Hunter outlines from 20 blocks.

Default points: 100 per Hunter killed, 200 per Ghost killed, 50 per artifact, and 75 a minute as a dead player's artifact. The 2 to 8 Soul Orb range, the win bonus and the 100 to 700 score range are fixed in code.
Playing on as an artifact after dying is on by default. With it off, dead players go straight to spectating.

The play area is split into areas about 12 blocks wide, and the share of them holding an artifact grows with the number of Hunters: 25% plus 1/30 for each Hunter (plus 1), up to all of them at 22 or more Hunters.
There is a 'hunter death time' setting (25 ticks), but nothing uses it: a grab always takes 2.5 seconds.
Lag compensation is switched on by default, but its rewind cap is set to 300 nanoseconds, so in practice flashlight hits aren't rewound for your ping.
The 15 normal artifact items (Precious Gold, Heavy Anvil, Old Beef Jerky and more) and the 6 dead player artifact items are set per map.

guide.name: Copycat
guide.summary: A memory building game with no PvP. You study a build for 16 seconds, then some of its blocks vanish and you put them back from the items you're given. Each round more blocks go missing and you need a bigger share of them right, and anyone below the target is out. Soul Orbs come from how many rounds you survive.
guide.tokenLine: 2 to 8 by rounds survived, +1 for most points, max 9

beats.caption: Memorize it, then fill the gaps
beats.sub: You get 16 seconds to study the build. Then blocks vanish and you put them back from the items you're given.

beats.caption: Fall short and you're out
beats.sub: Round 1 needs 30% of your missing blocks right. The target rises every round, up to 75%.

beats.caption: Soul Orbs for rounds survived
beats.sub: 2 Soul Orbs, rising to 8 at 8 rounds survived. Whoever has the most points gets 1 more.

howToPlay.text: Join with /event join while the queue is open (90 seconds by default). Copycat needs only 1 player to start. You are sent to the Copycat lobby, and your inventory is saved and cleared, then given back when the game ends.

Everyone gets their own walled plot with a black terracotta floor. You are shrunk to half size and can fly, and if you fly out of your plot you are teleported back in. You can't take damage, get hungry, die or drop items.

Each round starts with "Round N, Memorize the build!" and the same build appears in every plot, turned to a random side. You get 16 seconds to study it and can't touch it yet. The build's footprint is marked on your floor in light gray terracotta.

Then "Go!" shows how many blocks went missing, how long you have and what share you need right. The missing blocks vanish from your plot and your inventory is filled with exactly the items for them, plus a lime dye called "I'm done!" in hotbar slot 9.

Only blocks with at least 1 side open to air can go missing, so blocks buried inside the build never do. A door or tall flower goes missing as a whole. The face resting on the ground doesn't count as open unless the build floats.

Put the blocks back where they were. You can only place and break inside the build's own area ("Stay inside the marked build area"). Breaking is instant and gives the block back to your inventory, nothing drops.

When your copy is perfect it locks itself straight away ("Perfect!") and chat tells everyone. You can also lock it early by left clicking "I'm done!" twice quickly. Either way you can't change it after that. Submitting turns you into an invisible spectator who can fly around the arena until the round ends.

The round ends when the timer runs out or when every builder has locked in. Your plot is then checked and chat tells you your points and what share of your missing blocks you got right, against what you needed.
If your share is below the target, you are eliminated. If every builder misses the target in the same round, nobody is eliminated and chat says everyone gets another chance.

Next everyone is moved around to look at the round's best 2 builds and up to 2 of the worst failed ones, 7 seconds each. After that the eliminated players are announced and become invisible spectators who can fly around the arena but can't touch anything.
After a 5 second break ("Faster!") your plot is cleared and the next round starts with a new build. Each build is only used once per game.

The game ends when only 1 builder is left, when no builders are left, after 20 rounds, or when the server runs out of builds. The player with the most points is shown as the winner, the top 5 are listed in chat, and 5 seconds later everyone goes back to the lobby.

scoring.text: Survival only looks at your missing blocks: how many you put back correctly, out of how many went missing. Wrong or extra blocks never count against survival, they only cost points.
Each missing block you put back correctly is 10 points.

You lose 5 points for every block that is there but wrong (in a missing spot or one of the build's own blocks you swapped), 5 for every one of the build's own blocks you broke and left empty, and 5 for every extra block placed where the build has nothing.
A perfect copy (nothing missing, wrong, removed or extra) adds 50 points, plus 1 point for every second left on the timer when it locked in.

A block counts as right if it's the same block, with the same top or bottom half for stairs, slabs and closed trapdoors, the same number of candles, sea pickles, snow layers or turtle eggs, and the same waterlogging. Which way it faces is not checked. Heads and banners must have the same skin or pattern, and you're given the exact item.

Example: a round 1 build with 10 missing blocks gives you 25 seconds (at the default 2.5 seconds per block), and you need 3 right (30%). 8 right and 1 wrong is 80% and 75 points. 2 right is only 20%, so you're out.

tips.text: Your items are a cheat sheet: you are given exactly what went missing, so the blocks in your inventory tell you what to look for, and an empty inventory (apart from "I'm done!") means everything is placed.
During the 16 seconds, focus on the outside of the build. Blocks with no side open to air can never go missing.
Never leave a spot empty if you have a guess. A right guess is 10 points and counts toward survival, and a wrong one only costs 5 points and doesn't hurt your survival share.

Don't spend time turning blocks the right way. Facing isn't checked, but top or bottom half is for stairs, slabs and closed trapdoors, and so is how many candles, sea pickles or snow layers are in a spot.
Leave the build's own blocks alone. Breaking one and not putting it back costs 5 points, and so does any block placed where the build has none.

You don't need to press "I'm done!" for the speed bonus. A perfect copy locks itself the moment it's finished, and the clock stops for the bonus right then. Submitting an imperfect copy just gives up the time you had left to fix it.
Fixing a mistake is cheap: breaking is instant and the block goes straight back into your inventory.
Don't go idle. A builder who doesn't move for 90 seconds is removed and gets no Soul Orbs.

quirks.text: The winner and the +1 Soul Orb go to whoever has the most points, which isn't always the last builder standing.
The game stops as soon as only 1 builder is left, so the last survivor doesn't play extra rounds. Their rounds survived is however many rounds were played.
Elimination waits until after the showcase, so a player who failed can still be shown in the worst builds before being knocked out.
A double slab counts as the full block it's made of, so 2 oak slabs in one spot match oak planks. Smooth stone is the exception.
An open trapdoor matches whether it is hinged at the top or the bottom.
Right clicking a chest, crafting table, sign or other block with a menu does nothing in the arena. Sneak with an item in hand to place a block against it.
Water and lava don't flow, fire can't be lit or spread, and leaves don't decay anywhere in the arena.
Water, lava and waterlogged blocks go back with buckets: you're given a bucket for each one that went missing.

config.text: Copycat isn't in the default list of games that start automatically, so staff start it.
The lobby and the corner the plot grid grows from are set per map.
Build time is 2.5 seconds per missing block and the game lasts at most 20 rounds by default.

The builds are schematic files on the server, up to 16 by 16 by 16 blocks. Each one can be set to float above the floor, get a minimum or maximum build time, or have block types that never go missing. By default only mini_skyblock.schem has a setting: it floats.
The 16 second memorize time, how many blocks go missing, the survival targets and the point values are fixed in the code, not the config.
